nodes.name: EdGraphNode_Comment_5
nodes.title: EdGraphNode_Comment
nodes.comment:
The "TurnYawWeight" curve is set to 1 in TurnInPlace animations, so its current value from GetCurveValue will be the current weight of the TurnInPlace animation. 
We can use this to "unweight" the TurnInPlace animation to get the full RemainingTurnYaw curve value.

nodes.name: EdGraphNode_Comment_6
nodes.title: EdGraphNode_Comment
nodes.comment: Avoid applying the curve delta when the curve first becomes relevant. E.g. When a turn animation starts, the previous curve value will be 0 and the current value will be 90, but no actual rotation has happened yet.

nodes.name: EdGraphNode_Comment_7
nodes.title: EdGraphNode_Comment
nodes.comment: Reduce the root yaw offset by the amount of rotation from the turn animation.

nodes.name: EdGraphNode_Comment_3
nodes.title: EdGraphNode_Comment
nodes.comment:
TurnInPlace #5\r
When the yaw offset gets too big, we trigger TurnInPlace animations to rotate the character back. E.g. if the camera is rotated 90 degrees to the right, it will be facing the character\'s right shoulder. If we play an animation that rotates the character 90 degrees to the left, the character will once again be facing away from the camera.\r
We use the "TurnYawAnimModifier" animation modifier to generate the necessary curves on each TurnInPlace animation.\r
See ABP_ItemAnimLayersBase for examples of triggering TurnInPlace animations.
